content.title: Texas Children’s Houston Open Purse: How Much Does the Winner Make?
content.text: 2.2K Views 0 Shares Updated Mar 29, 2026 at 6:02pm Getty A detailed view of the trophy on the first tee during the first round of the Texas Children's Houston Open at Memorial Park Golf Course on March 28, 2024. The Texas Children’s Houston Open continues to solidify its place as a key stop on the PGA Tour calendar – not just because of its timing ahead of the Masters, but also due to its increasingly lucrative purse. In 2026, the tournament boasts a total prize pool of $9.9 million, marking another step forward in the event’s financial growth. That number represents a steady climb from recent years, including a $9.5 million purse in 2025 and $9.1 million in 2024. The upward trend reflects the PGA Tour’s broader push to increase player earnings and remain competitive in the evolving global golf landscape. While the Houston Open is not classified as a Signature Event, its purse still rivals many mid-tier tournaments and provides a significant payday opportunity for players across the field. For the winner, the stakes are especially high. The 2026 champion is set to earn approximately $1.78 million, along with 500 FedEx Cup points and valuable exemptions into future events. That combination of financial reward and competitive advantage makes the Houston Open more than just a warm-up; it’s a pivotal opportunity.
